# Contribution Guidelines

## General Contribution Framework

The TenX platform welcomes contributions from developers following established open-source principles similar to those implemented by leading LMS platforms. Drawing from the Moodle contribution model, all contributions to TenX must be released under appropriate licensing agreements that ensure the platform's continued open development[1](https://docs.moodle.org/en/MoodleDocs:Guidelines_for_contributors). Contributors are encouraged to identify areas for improvement in content, functionality, grammar, or formatting and actively participate in enhancing the platform's capabilities.  
The contribution process requires proper authentication and authorization, with contributors needing to establish appropriate access credentials before making any modifications to the codebase[1](https://docs.moodle.org/en/MoodleDocs:Guidelines_for_contributors). This security-first approach ensures that all contributions maintain the platform's integrity while facilitating collaborative development. Contributors should focus on areas where they can add meaningful value, whether through bug fixes, feature enhancements, documentation improvements, or user experience optimizations.

## Documentation and Visual Standards

Visual documentation plays a crucial role in the TenX contribution process, with contributors encouraged to include comprehensive screenshots and visual aids to support their documentation efforts[1](https://docs.moodle.org/en/MoodleDocs:Guidelines_for_contributors). The platform maintains strict adherence to its established design system, which serves as the foundation for all visual and interface contributions[4](https://shaficassim.com/portfolio/design-system/). This design system encompasses a comprehensive set of standards that promote consistency across the platform through reusable components and established design patterns.  
The TenX Design System functions as both a styleguide and a toolkit, providing codified standards for visual elements, interaction patterns, and user interface components[4](https://shaficassim.com/portfolio/design-system/). Contributors working on interface elements must reference these established patterns to ensure consistency across the platform. The design system covers critical elements including typography, iconography, color schemes, headers and footers, spacing and grid systems, messaging frameworks, data tables, button designs, lightboxes, and tooltips.

## Code Quality and Development Standards

TenX maintains rigorous code quality standards that must be followed by all contributors. The platform requires minimal code duplication, with any necessary duplication properly justified and documented[5](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65d35b01a4034b72499019e8/66459d3e444019e25078b9a8_ChainSecurity_TenX_compressed.pdf). All external libraries must be properly referenced as package dependencies, including specific version compatibility information, ensuring that no library files are mixed with TenX's proprietary code.  
Compilation standards require that all contributed code compiles successfully with the latest Solidity compiler version, or if older versions are used, the reasons must be thoroughly documented[5](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65d35b01a4034b72499019e8/66459d3e444019e25078b9a8_ChainSecurity_TenX_compressed.pdf). The platform maintains a zero-tolerance policy for compiler warnings unless such warnings are explicitly documented and justified. These standards ensure that the codebase remains maintainable, secure, and compatible with evolving blockchain technologies.

## Testing and Quality Assurance

Contributors must participate in comprehensive testing protocols that include bug reporting through designated tracking systems and participation in quality assurance testing procedures[2](https://support.moodle.com/support/solutions/articles/80001075416-how-to-support-and-contribute-to-moodle). The testing framework requires thorough validation of all contributed code, with particular attention to security implications and system integration compatibility. Contributors are expected to perform usability testing and report results through established communication channels.
